security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline filenames, CSS, comments, or JavaScript RegExp.exec. The real issues are low-severity external network dependencies for p5.js and Google Fonts in the generated viewer template; no prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or command execution evidence was found.

remediation.issue: Generated artifacts load p5.js and Google Fonts from third-party CDNs.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle approved local copies, pin resources with integrity controls where possible, or clearly disclose the network dependency before generated artifacts run.

content.value_statement: Creating polished generative art usually requires both visual direction and working creative code. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to produce p5.js artworks with seeded variation and controls.
actual_capabilities: Creates an algorithmic philosophy before implementation.
Generates self-contained p5.js HTML artifacts for browsers and Claude artifacts.
Uses seeded randomness so the same seed reproduces the same artwork.
Adds parameter controls for exploring visual variations.
Provides a reusable viewer template with sidebar controls and download support.
Encourages original visual systems instead of copying known artists.
limitations: Generated art depends on the model quality and prompt detail.
The viewer template loads p5.js and fonts from external CDNs unless modified.
Complex animations may need manual performance tuning for slower devices.
It does not replace legal review for commercial art licensing questions.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Generative Artwork
use_cases.description: Turn a visual idea into a reproducible p5.js sketch with controls and seed navigation.

use_cases.title: Build Interactive Visual Assets
use_cases.description: Create browser-ready art artifacts for presentations, portfolios, or product explorations.

use_cases.title: Explore Computational Aesthetics
use_cases.description: Study how particles, fields, noise, and parameters can express a visual concept.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Simple Artwork
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a complete first artifact.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an original algorithmic artwork inspired by flowing water. Include a short philosophy and a self-contained p5.js HTML artifact with seed controls.

prompt_templates.title: Add Specific Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Create generative art based on wind patterns. Add controls for particle count, turbulence, trail length, and palette intensity.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Reproducible Series
prompt_templates.scenario: User wants multiple variations from one system.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design one algorithmic art system for crystalline growth. Show how seeds 1 through 5 create distinct but related variations.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Sophisticated Conceptual Piece
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an original p5.js generative artwork about memory decay. Use subtle references in the algorithm, avoid literal symbols, and make the parameter controls support careful exploration.

output_examples.input: Create generative art inspired by forest mycelium.
output_examples.output: A concise philosophy about hidden networks, followed by an interactive artwork with branching growth, seeded variation, and controls for density and spread.

output_examples.input: Make an animated abstract piece with calm motion.
output_examples.output: A browser-ready p5.js artifact with slow field motion, soft colors, seed navigation, and sliders for speed, flow scale, and particle count.

output_examples.input: Give me 100 variations of the same system.
output_examples.output: A single seeded artwork system that lets the user jump between seed values and explore consistent variations without separate files.

best_practices: Start with a clear visual concept and let the algorithm express that concept.
Use seed controls when you need reproducible variations or a collectible series.
Review generated HTML before sharing it, especially external script and font links.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for copies of a living artist or copyrighted style.
Do not remove seed controls if reproducibility matters.
Do not add too many sliders when a few meaningful parameters are clearer.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates original p5.js generative art with a philosophy, seeded randomness, and interactive controls.

faq.question: Can I reproduce the same image later?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill emphasizes seeded randomness, so the same seed should produce the same result.

faq.question: Does the output work outside Claude?
faq.answer: Yes. The intended output is a self-contained HTML artifact that can run in a browser.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: The default template loads p5.js and Google Fonts from external CDNs, so offline use needs local replacements.

faq.question: Can it make animated artwork?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports both static and animated p5.js systems when the prompt asks for motion.

faq.question: Is it safe to request a known artist style?
faq.answer: No. The skill directs users toward original algorithmic concepts instead of copying existing artists.
